tasks.title: FIELD spatial-audio launch
tasks.prompt:
Build FIELD, a complete spatial-audio headphone launch website, from the supplied blank scaffold and original asset bundle. The site should feel like one connected motion experience, not a stack of sections with fade-ins.

Begin with a strong typographic/product composition. Scroll carries the same product into an exploded technical view. A recognizable signal passes through the driver into a full-screen listening environment, then through a horizontal sequence of listening spaces. Later that signal becomes an interactive waveform/playhead. Finish by reassembling the currently configured product and exporting its actual selected settings as JSON.

Use motion to explain how the product and listening modes relate. Keep important labels attached to their parts. A visitor must be able to follow the selected component and signal through changes of scale, camera, layout, and renderer. Use the approved assets and content, but author the page composition and animation yourself. The static design must also be coherent and usable.

Visitors will reverse scroll, skip chapters, change the listening mode while motion is active, drag the waveform, resize, and use keyboard controls. The latest choice must survive those actions. Reaching the same chapter and selected configuration by different history-independent paths should produce the same meaningful scene after settling. An intentional direct scrub may jump; a stale animation must not overwrite newer input.

Make desktop and mobile compositions deliberate. Reduced motion must preserve meaning and function. Do not require a personal account or external service. Do not add more decorative motion instead of completing the experience. Use the available browser tools to inspect the actual running result and refine what needs work. Preserve an initial working checkpoint, your final source, and evidence of the important journeys.

tasks.title: NORTHSTAR modular-travel commerce
tasks.prompt:
Build NORTHSTAR, a complete collection-to-cart site for modular travel bags, from the supplied blank scaffold and original product silhouette. Start with a deliberate collection composition. Filtering and reordering must carry the selected product into a gallery-to-detail transition; variant changes must stay attached to that same product, and adding it must visibly reconcile the detail view, cart count, and responsive cart sheet.

Use motion to explain product continuity rather than decorating independent cards. Visitors will reverse filters, choose another item while a transition is active, switch variants, open and close the cart rapidly, resize, and use the keyboard. Latest input wins. The same selected item and variant reached through different history-independent paths must settle to the same meaningful view and export.

Make desktop and mobile layouts intentional and preserve all function under reduced motion. Use ordinary browser inspection to refine the actual result. Preserve an initial working checkpoint, final source, and evidence for selection, reversal, cart, export, mobile, and reduced-motion journeys.

tasks.title: FRAMECUT creative timeline editor
tasks.prompt:
Build FRAMECUT, a complete single-page creative timeline editor, from the supplied blank scaffold and original glyph sheet. The timeline, playhead, canvas selection, transform overlay, and inspector must behave like one system. Selecting and rearranging clips, changing zoom, scrubbing, undoing, and resizing must preserve the current selection and keep its overlay attached to the rendered object.

Use motion to explain edits, selection, and time. Visitors will reverse a rearrangement, select another object while a transition is active, drag the playhead in both directions, zoom, resize, invoke undo, and use the keyboard. Latest input wins; stale work must not overwrite the current edit. Equivalent history-independent paths must settle to the same selected clip and exportable project state.

Make desktop and mobile editor compositions deliberate and preserve meaning and function under reduced motion. Use ordinary browser inspection to refine the actual result. Preserve an initial working checkpoint, final source, and evidence for selection, attachment, interruption, undo, export, mobile, and reduced-motion journeys.
